- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early/medium horizon (first 10–15 days) — reduce forecast by 1–2% for short-term (0–15d) to correct for overconfidence.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — dampen forecast by 3–5% in 10–20d window following spikes.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — if last 5 days show high variance, reduce forecast amplitude by 10–15% to avoid overfitting.
- Model fails to capture “low-activity” periods — if 3+ consecutive days are below 70, forecast should be capped at 70–72 to avoid downward drift.
- Model tends to lag in correcting for true price drops — if true outcome drops below 70, forecast should be adjusted downward by 2–4% per day until stabilization.
